80: I carry heavy bags to lovely rooms. The bags are not mine. The rooms are not mine. The stairs are all mine.
81: Today I carried a suitcase heavier than I am. Inside, the guest told me, were rocks. Only rocks.
82: Guests thank me and close the door. I stand in the hallway a moment, then carry my empty hands back down the stairs.
83: A guest packed for a weekend and brought nine bags. I did not ask. I simply carried, and I grew stronger.
84: I have carried every kind of bag up every kind of stair. My arms know this hotel better than I do.
85: People tip me for carrying things they could carry themselves. I do not complain. I am just out of breath.
86: I know which rooms have the good windows. I stand in them briefly, holding a stranger's coat, and I dream.
87: A guest asked me to carry a bag very carefully. It was empty. I carried it with great respect anyway.
88: My job is to move other people's things to nicer places than I will ever sleep. I do not mind. Much.
89: Guests hand me their bags without ever looking up. I have carried the belongings of people who never saw my face.
90: Someone handed me a bag and said be careful, it is fragile. Then it barked. I remain professional at all times.
91: I carry, I climb, I knock, I leave. Somewhere in a lovely room a bag I carried is finally resting. Lucky bag.
92: The heavier the bag, the longer the hallway becomes. I have measured this many times. Science keeps disagreeing.
93: I have opened a thousand doors for other people. I hold them, I smile, I watch others walk through. It is fine.
94: A guest brought a bag full of sand. For the beach, they said. The beach is outside, full of sand. I said nothing.
95: I carry things up. Gravity carries things down. Between us, gravity is winning, and it does no lifting at all.
96: My arms are the strongest part of me. My back files a formal complaint at the end of every single shift.
97: I have carried luggage for people going everywhere. I mostly go up four floors and then back down again.
98: A guest asked me to carry two heavy bags in one hand so they could film it. I obliged. My hand did not forgive me.
99: I set a heavy case down in a fine room, and for one moment it was my room. Then I closed the door from outside.
100: I solve mysteries here at the hotel. Mostly whose towels these are. It's steady work.
101: You chase thieves across the whole world. I once found a missing slipper. Under the bed.
102: I'm the detective for this one building. My whole territory ends at the parking lot.
103: A world detective, and then there's me. I know which guest quietly takes two breakfasts.
104: My biggest case this year was a lamp that walked off. It was, it turns out, in storage.
105: I guard the whole hotel. Four floors. Five, if you count the roof, which nobody visits.
106: People bring me their problems. Usually a squeaky door. I write it in my big serious notebook.
107: I've cracked every case in this lobby. There have been two. Both were about umbrellas.
108: I keep the peace across the entire hotel. My hardest days involve the ice machine.
109: I wear the coat, I have the badge. It says House Detective. The house is not very big.
110: You solve crimes on six continents. I investigate who keeps taking the good pens.
111: My beat is the hallway. I know every creak in it. I have named a few of the creaks.
112: I once tailed a suspicious guest all the way to the elevator. Then it closed. Case paused.
113: I'm on duty day and night. Mostly day. The night detective is a lamp at the front desk.
114: I investigate. I deduce. Last week I deduced the vending machine ate a coin. It had.
115: The hotel trusts me with its greatest secrets. So far: the pool is heated. Barely.
116: I keep a careful list of suspects. It is the same guest who complains about the pillows.
117: My office is a small room behind the desk. I've nearly solved the mystery of its smell.
118: I've patrolled here for years. I could find room 12 blindfolded. It's next to room 11.
119: Some detectives get a whole city. I got one hotel. I have investigated every square of its carpet.
